title: Ghost prefill & KV eviction — weekly synthesis
content:
Weekly sync — 2028-04-04 to 2028-04-06
Attendees: Maya, Diego, Priya, Liam, Samira (oncall check-in)
Context: Running synthesis from last sprint's kernel prefetch patch (PR 2147). We observed intermittent KV cache evictions that correlate with rare scheduling decisions when the micro-batching scheduler moves hot requests between lanes. Team asked for a single-note summary and a prioritized action list.

Top-level summary:
- Root symptom: short-lived KV entries (1–3s) that should have lasted ~30s under current TTL profile; leads to p99 tail jumps in multi-turn chat workloads (p99 up from 210ms -> 380ms under synthetic spikes).
- Reproducible pattern: warm-started sessions seeing "cold prefill" behavior after a lane reassignment inside the kernel. We call this "ghost prefill" (cache looked warm, but kernel triggered prefill path and replaced small-on-kv slots).
- Impact: affects Dedicated customers with high session affinity and high sequence length variance; estimated 3–7% request cost increase for affected workloads due to missed KV hits.

What we validated this week:
- Logged kernel trace (sampling) around lane handoff events; confirmed that on lane-move, KV eviction call executes before affinity metadata is re-bound. (Diego)
- Micro-batching scheduler unit tests expanded to assert KV handle "lease" across lane moves — tests exposed a race (test added in PR 2147). (Priya)
- Benchmarks: ran a 10k-session synthetic with alternating short/long requests; baseline (no lane moves) p50=78ms p99=210ms; with induced lane moves p50=86ms p99=372ms. Observed +12% p50 and +77% p99.
- Memory/eviction metrics: KV store eviction count spiked precisely at lane-change markers; eviction TTL not obeyed in ~12% of cases where an active prefill had been in-flight.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kernel scheduling emits a teardown event that triggers a local KV orphan-cleanup callback before the new owner attaches — race window ~5–40ms.
2) Prefill path assumes exclusive KV ownership and forcibly replaces small segments to avoid double-fetch; this logic didn't consider handoffs.
3) Batching coalescer can re-order request sequences during congestion, creating a temporary key namespace mismatch (less likely based on traces).

Immediate experiments planned (short-lived, 48–72h):
- Experiment A (safety): Delay local eviction callback by 75ms after lane teardown if a prefill marker exists. Objective: see if p99 reduces without causing memory pressure. Owner: Diego. DUE: 2028-04-07.
- Experiment B (logic): Make prefill atomic: attach 'pending-prefill' token to KV entries and prevent replacement until commit/abort. Objective: eliminate ghost replacements. Owner: Priya. DUE: 2028-04-09.
- Experiment C (ops): Increase KV TTL by 2x for sessions flagged as "high-turn" to force more robust hit rates while we fix logic. Owner: Ops (Liam to coordinate). DUE: 2028-04-05 (hotfix window).

Data & checkpoints to collect during experiments:
- p50/p95/p99 for the synthetic alternating workload every 10 minutes.
- KV eviction per-second and fraction of evictions with cause="hand_off_teardown".
- Kernel trace sampling (1%) with lane move markers; correlate with eviction ids.

Decisions made in this doc:
- Rolling back PR 2147 is NOT acceptable at scale because it improves prefill latency for the majority of customers; instead we'll ship a targeted patch.
- Prioritize Experiment A first (low risk), then B (medium). Ops hotfix (C) goes live immediately for affected clusters.

Open action items (owner, ETA):
- Diego: implement delayed-eviction flag and run A/B against staging clusters; post results in Slack; ETA 2028-04-07.
- Priya: branch atomic-prefill prototype and add invariant tests; file RFC for API-level token; ETA 2028-04-09.
- Liam: schedule ops hotfix window and rollback plan; notify customers flagged in RW-11234; ETA 2028-04-05.
- Samira (oncall): add a runbook snippet to the coalescer playbook describing ghost-prefill detection and mitigation steps. ETA 2028-04-06.
- Maya: prepare a short customer-facing note for CS describing the issue and mitigations (non-technical) after Experiment A results. ETA 2028-04-10.

Oncall notes (things we observed overnight):
- 2028-04-04 02:14 UTC: Single Dedicated tenant experienced p99 spike coincident with a rolling kernel upgrade; correlated to a lane rebalancing event. Manual eviction observed. (Samira)
- 2028-04-05 19:02 UTC: A burst of small prompts (avg len 16 tokens) caused spike when mixing with long-latency completions (avg len 120 tokens) — pattern replicates synthetic test.

Quick wins and mitigations (<=24h):
- Ops TTL bump (C) for flagged tenants.
- Add ephemeral metric: "prefill_pending_count" exposed to dashboards to make the problem visible.
- Turn on 1% canary of delayed-eviction in staging to validate memory profile.

Risks & concerns:
- Delaying eviction increases temporary memory usage; need clear OOM guard rails on each host.
- Atomic prefill requires a consistent commit/abort path across microkernels — subtle and could affect throughput if not tuned.
- Customer communication needs to be tight; avoid promising hard SLAs until patch validated.

Notes to self / raw scratch stuff (keep as-is):
- grep kernel.log -n "lane-rebind" | sed -n '1,80p' -> saw handoff id 0x7f9c2b \n
- sample trace snippet: [1680654321.123] lane=12 evict(key=chat/uid/387) cause=hand_off_teardown prefill=1 
- local memory on host a5 exceeded soft limit once during test A (need mem-sampling)

Open questions for product/solutions:
- Should we expose a session-level hint (prefer-sticky) for customers who want absolute p99 stability at cost of less kernel packing? (Product)
- For Dedicated customers, is it acceptable to offer a toggle (strong-affinity) that locks sessions to a lane? (Sales/Customer-success)

Next sync cadence:
- Quick check-in: 2028-04-07 (status of Experiment A), 20min.
- Deep triage if A fails: 2028-04-09, 60min with SRE and Product.

Appendix: short trace sample (raw)
- [TRACE] 2028-04-04T02:14:03Z kernel: lane-move start id=0x7f9c2b session=387
- [TRACE] 2028-04-04T02:14:03Z kernel: prefill:start key=chat/uid/387 src=kv local=true
- [TRACE] 2028-04-04T02:14:03Z kernel: evict key=chat/uid/387 cause=hand_off_teardown
- [TRACE] 2028-04-04T02:14:03Z kernel: prefill:complete key=chat/uid/387 duration_ms=28

If you read only one thing: run experiment A on staging today and capture p99 delta. If we see >30% p99 reduction, promote logic fix to canary.

-- Maya (notes/triage)
